correctness.rationale: For the linear kernel, cross-MMD factors as the first-half mean difference A times the second-half mean difference B. The published studentizer reduces to \(B^2S/s^2\), so the statistic is \(\operatorname{sgn}(B)sA/\sqrt S\). Under the equal-variance Gaussian null, the first-half pooled statistic is exactly \(t_{2s-2}\), while the independent sign of B preserves symmetry, yielding \(\sqrt{s/(s-1)}t_{2s-2}\). The exact cutoff and finite-size anti-conservatism follow, and the quoted tail expansion/numerics were independently checked.

originality.rationale: The source paper explicitly defines cross-MMD as a sample-split inner product and its studentizer as the sample variance of projected first-half variables. Specializing those published formulas to the linear kernel immediately factors out the second-half mean difference and leaves, up to a deterministic scale and independent sign, the classical pooled equal-variance two-sample t statistic. Thus the exact finite t law and exact t cutoff are direct textbook consequences of the published statistic definition; the first-order tail correction is then a standard Student-vs-normal expansion. The absence of this special case in the source text does not overcome implication coverage.
